paper_title: Separating Measurement Failures from Defence Failures in Split Language-Model Privacy

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Split-training privacy evaluations fail through distinct mechanisms. Evaluators can overlook an exposed gradient channel, align reconstructions against shifted labels, or deploy uncalibrated probes before testing a candidate defence, while calibrated attacks can also refute real defences. Separating these failure modes alters which claims survive. We conduct a retrospective evidentiary reanalysis across four split-LLM campaigns and two cross-cutting scope checks covering host key custody and variational mutual-information bounds, mapping every recorded claim to one of five admissibility states (breach, non-detection, undetermined coverage, invalid measurement, or out-of-scope inference). Across a 19-configuration exploration, only four of 24 required probes qualified, yet those four calibrated probes still established qualified privacy breaches in 13 configurations, while utility or learning-gain failures eliminated the remaining 6. In a seven-cell defence-redesign pilot, 2 quantised configurations failed utility gates, calibrated next-byte structure probes breached the 0.02 gate on all 7 cells (0.097 to 0.112), and qualified punctuation-property probes reached 0.79 to 0.89, yielding 4 failed and 3 undetermined composite privacy assessments (the latter from marginal null-band excursions on punctuation bindings). Negative evidence against both defence families remains intact. Scope checks further show that shared-key orthogonal wrappers protect passive network captures without hiding activations from a compromised restoring host, and why near-zero variational lower bounds leave worst-case leakage unconstrained. Rerunnable scripts verify 1,522 checks across 122 SHA-256-pinned artifacts while preserving each campaign's native seed intervals and retrospective boundaries.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.content: Split learning partitions neural network between local client and remote server so raw training text stays on the client device [23, 9]. Intermediate activations and returned loss gradients still cross that boundary. Gradient and representation inversion attacks recover private tokens from both exchanged tensors [27, 15, 12], and deeper cut points retain recoverable internal states [4, 5, 13]. Interpreting any reported recovery score requires exact experimental context. Attack outcomes shift substantially with the messages an adversary observes, the pretrained or fine-tuned weights and cryptographic keys it possesses, the token index it targets, and the calibration controls backing the evaluator [10, 24, 25]. Recent empirical studies expose individual pieces of this measurement problem. Omitting clientreturned gradient channel invalidates privacy assurance derived from forward activations alone [17], while adding backward gradients shifts exact-document recovery far more sharply than average token accuracy [19]. Choice of aggregation unit alters the substantive conclusion. Although LLM-Attack Suite standardises observation contracts, undefended controls, and saved predictions [16], and Smith et al. [20] show how adaptive optimisation and evaluator choices reshape inversion tradeoffs, multi-campaign studies still require explicit rules reconciling conflicting claims. Empirical privacy auditing in differential privacy similarly separates valid lower bounds on leakage from unproven upper assurances [7]. 1 This paper re-examines four split-LLM training campaigns and two cross-cutting security claims drawn from one research programme. Individual campaigns investigate decoy-padded gradients, shifted token labels in boundary-replacement study, incomplete probe qualification across 19-cell exploration, and calibrated seven-cell defence-redesign pilot. Each campaign failed for distinct reason. Two companion scope analyses then test whether shared-key orthogonal wrappers withstand compromised restoring host [22] and whether near-zero variational mutual-information readouts bound worst-case leakage [1, 11, 21]. Shared corpora and sequential design choices require keeping each campaigns native estimand and seed unit separate. Our reanalysis traces every headline statement from the adversarys observation surface back to the primary generated tables. Five admissibility outcomes separate confirmed breaches from non-detection, undetermined coverage, invalid targets, and out-of-scope threat transfers. Distinguishing broken probes from broken defences matters. Executable scripts reconstruct 76 configuration-by-seed contrasts from the exploration alongside paired losses and candidate probe advantages from 66 defence-pilot runs and verify 1,522 internal checks across 122 SHA-256-pinned artifacts [18]. Archived session-identity logs, throughput timings, and key-derivation manifests bound what shared-key rotation achieves in practice, while an analytic lower-bound argument delimits variational mutual-information readouts.

sections.title: 2 Scope and retrospective admissibility framework
sections.content: A stated privacy claim paired with its supporting experimental records forms our basic unit of analysis. Scope covers four training campaigns and two security-transfer arguments. Because we selected these episodes from an earlier programme synthesis whose outcomes were already known, the resulting archive traces how local measurements grew into sweeping claims while leaving field-wide error rates unestimated. Component results remain credited to their originating studies, and Table 1 summarises how each recorded headline maps onto its admitted evidentiary state. All historical runs finished before we specified this reconciliation. Throughout the text, frozen exploratory protocols, completed pilot executions, unexecuted confirmation proposals, and secondary consistency checks remain explicitly separated. Our analysis recomputes stored loss contrasts, probe advantages, and decision thresholds directly from archived tables without retraining victim models or fitting stronger attackers. Prospective validation requires an independent cohort. Where LLM-Attack Suite defines observation contracts and control conventions [16], we apply its reporting structure to compare cross-campaign claims under their original experimental budgets. Evidence required for claim. Evaluating any candidate claim begins by logging the split protocol, victim cohort, secret-key custody, remote host state, and observable tensor channels. Target indexing and control bindings come next. Specifically, each record pairs the protected token or property target with its exact tensor index, training horizon, baseline guesser, acceptance gate, and independent resampling unit. qualification binding ties positive canary floors and permutation-null bands to one concrete target, channel, defence family, and probe implementation. Passing controls on one channel leaves unmeasured channels unqualified. Primary generated CSV and JSON outputs alongside active collection manifests supersede informal narrative summaries. Whenever subsequent technical review revises an earlier disposition, we report both the updated status and every attached operational caveat regardless of which reading looks more favourable. Every retained number carries explicit provenance. Appendix binds each quantity to its SHA-256-hashed file path and marks whether our scripts recomputed the statistic from raw seed records or extracted it from cited study. Five admissibility outcomes for specified claim. often merit distinct evidentiary labels. Individual endpoints within single split configuration 2 Breach. An admissible, calibrated probe exceeds its frozen acceptance threshold and establishes leakage for the specified observer, target, and finite protocol. Unprobed disclosures may still coexist alongside it. Non-detection. calibrated attack stays within its acceptance rule under the tested architecture, dataset, and optimisation budget. Consistent with empirical differential-privacy auditing [7], staying below an attack threshold leaves worst-case mutual information and adaptive recovery unbounded from above. Undetermined. Missing coverage or failed controls block privacy passes. Invalid. verified implementation defect severs the recorded score from the claimed estimand, as occurs when next-token predictions are misread as current-token reconstructions. Properly relabelled, the underlying number may remain informative. Out-of-scope. Transferring measurement to stronger observer, altered key-custody regime, or untested protocol exceeds what the original experiment can support. Utility loss and causal remote-learning gain are tracked alongside privacy under each campaigns original conjunctive decision rule. Conjunctive gating acts asymmetrically across endpoints. Within the 19-cell exploration, one qualified breach or one utility failure suffices to reject candidate even when companion probes remain undetermined, whereas incomplete qualification alone blocks any joint privacy pass. Failing an exploratory remote-gain threshold similarly leaves population learning benefit unconfirmed on that split. Transferring conclusion. Carrying an empirical privacy result into new deployment setting requires matching protocols, secret-key custody, observed tensors, target alignments, and calibrated probe bindings. Wire confidentiality differs sharply from host confidentiality. When an authorised server holds shared orthogonal key to restore activations in memory, passive wire non-detection says nothing about compromised host reading its own RAM [22]. Correlated token positions within fixed evaluation panels likewise add zero independent training seeds and restrict how far finite exploratory intervals generalise.

sections.title: 3.1 The decoy-gradient experiment
sections.content: Padding batches with synthetic decoy rows aims to obscure which activation vectors correspond to real user tokens [17]. During each split step, the trusted client transmits protected forward activations to the cloud, receives remote hidden states, evaluates the private training loss locally, and sends output gradients back to the cloud (decoy-gradient records). Decoy rows receive identically zero gradient. Because the local loss ignores synthetic positions, that deterministic zero-support mask exposes the exact real-versus-decoy row partition without revealing token identities directly, much as gradient-sparsity patterns leak metadata in federated vision and trajectory settings [27, 2]. Archived logs document exact partition recovery across all 4,096 inspected frames per run over nine training seeds (decoy-gradient records). Recovering token identities requires separate content attack. On that distinct token denominator, frequent-word probe beats constant-guess baseline by +0.65 to +1.50 pp. Across six utility-compliant cells that expose backward gradients (three seeds on each of two datasets), forward-activation probes stay inside the +1.0 pp privacy gate fixed prior to execution, whereas joint forward-and-backward evaluators breach that gate decisively. Forward-only non-detection remains accurate for an observer restricted to forward activations. Extending that assurance to the clouds actual bidirectional view constitutes an out-of-scope inference that the recorded backward breach refutes. Each row pairs the evaluated observation surface and initial claim with the admitted evidentiary state from Section 2 and its retained quantitative basis (pp denotes percentage points; MINE denotes Mutual Information Neural Estimation [1]). Hyperlinked record names point to the SHA-256-hashed provenance entries in Appendix A. partition leak across all 1,024 inspected frames per run over three mitigation seeds (producing 0.400 partition agreement at 32/80 base rate) while imposing roughly 0.01 nats of held-out cross-entropy utility cost (decoy-gradient records). That 0.01-nat figure measures validation loss degradation on the held-out split, while multi-step gradient accumulation and exact batch-reconstruction attacks [15, 12] remain untested against the noisy channel. Even within that bounded probe scope, closing deterministic support leak via per-row clipping and noise refutes blanket claims that perturbation mechanisms never mitigate training-time leakage.

sections.title: 3.2 The boundary-replacement review
sections.content: Reviewing the boundary-replacement codebase uncovered an off-by-one indexing shift between captured representations and target token IDs (boundary-review records). Hidden states for (x1, . . . , xT 1) met labels (x2, . . . , xT ). Every activation row encoding current token xt was consequently evaluated on how accurately probe predicted the subsequent token xt+1. High canary scores under that shifted alignment validate next-token predictive signal alone and invalidate claims of resistance to current-token input reconstruction, 4 though the raw numbers remain interpretable if explicitly relabelled as next-token probes. Independent evidence-review records from the same study also re-examined whether remote computation improved model quality (boundary-review records). Source-reported comparisons across six clean corpusand-seed pairs show that standalone client baselines trained from scratch with zero remote return outperform the split-trained remote model every time. Learned remote layers were consequently unnecessary for those evaluated endpoints. Zeroing the return pathway of an already trained split checkpoint tests different counterfactual, since co-adapted client layers naturally degrade when their expected remote input disappears mid-inference. Checkpoint-level scoring exposed an equally sharp divergence between continuous loss and discrete generation metrics (boundary-review records). Continuous loss cleared its threshold. Held-out negative log-likelihood rose by roughly 0.034 nats within rule, yet teacher-forced top-1 match on answer tokens dropped 16.64 pp from 34.79% to 18.15%. Answer-token matching under teacher forcing differs from standard multi-choice benchmark accuracy and comes here from single reviewed checkpoint. Paired with the unmeasured current-token reconstruction risk, this discrepancy narrows both the delegation and utility conclusions supported by the archive.

sections.title: 3.3 The privacy, utility and gain exploration
sections.content: Across 232 training runs spanning 19 candidate configurations and four seeds per cell, the exploratory trilemma campaign rejected every configuration under its frozen rules (exploration records). Recomputing the cell summary yields 13 qualified privacy breaches, 5 utility failures, and 7 remote-gain failures. Rejection causes overlap across cells. All 6 configurations whose privacy status remained undetermined failed utility or learning-gain gates independently, including width-64 on gain alone. Only four of the 24 required privacy probes passed pre-test qualification. Those four calibrated instruments consisted of input-byte probes operating on inbound and outbound gradients across the two evaluated defence families (exploration records). Unqualified probes prevent certifying joint privacy pass, yet breaches triggered by the four calibrated probes remain scientifically valid alongside the independent utility and gain failures. Boundary proximity on the span-6 cell illustrates why reanalysis scripts must check exact floatingpoint inequalities (exploration records). Across four training seeds, span-6 recorded mean utility delta of 0.0999705344 nats (2.95 105 nats inside the 0.10 limit) and an upper 95% Student-t bound of 0.1195024415 nats (inside the 0.12 cap). Both utility gates passed. Saved rejection flags instead trace to learning-gain failure paired with qualified byte-probe breach across four-seed exploratory cohort unadjusted for multiplicity. An accompanying confirmation proposal specified eight seeds per candidate (exploration records). Programme leads never froze, authorised, or ran that stage. Using plug-in exploratory means and variances, prospective calculation bounded whole-family confirmation power at 0.263772 (dropping sharply under wider variance multipliers) and served strictly as planning stop rule for future compute allocation.

sections.title: 3.4 The defence-redesign pilot
sections.content: Rebuilt probes drove subsequent seven-cell defence-redesign pilot comprising 66 runs across three paired seeds per cell and evaluation panels of 16,384 token windows (pilot records). Zero candidates achieved pilot eligibility. Every cell cleared the causal remote-gain gate and five cleared utility, whereas one-bit and two-bit activation quantisation failed their utility limits. Under the campaigns all-bindings aggregation policy, composite privacy assessments recorded 4 failures and 3 undetermined cells. Calibrated atomic probes nonetheless captured severe leakage across the tested quantisation and noise mechanisms (pilot records). Across qualified seed bindings, worst-seed sequence-property (punctuation5 fraction) correlation advantages spanned 0.79 to 0.89 against an acceptance ceiling of 0.02 (roughly 40 the gate), while next-byte structure (five-class accuracy) advantages reached 0.097 to 0.112 across all seven cells (roughly 5 the gate, with all 21 of 21 trained seed bindings qualified). Unlike Section 3.2, next-byte class served here as an intentional target. Observing calibrated probe advantages well above policy threshold refutes the candidate defences under that rule without implying probe malfunction. Recent split-LLM obfuscation studies report comparable persistence under perturbation-only defences [8, 3]. Calibration source files separate four numerical constants by role (pilot records). Positive-control canary floors sit at 0.10 for sequence properties (punctuation fraction) and 0.02 for next-byte structure targets, whereas both the permutation-null band and the candidate acceptance gate equal 0.02; semantic targets beyond byte classes were explicitly omitted from the pilot protocol. Passing canary floor confirms probe responsiveness on unprotected controls, and qualification logs record the four marginal null-band excursions on punctuation-property bindings (across three cells) as finite-sample variance on bounded exploratory panels.

sections.title: 4.1 Calibration coverage and reasons for rejection
sections.content: Our secondary analysis script rebuilds all 76 configuration-by-seed loss contrasts for the 19-cell exploration directly from archived metrics before verifying the published cell and seed summaries (exploration records). Pilot reconciliation follows parallel path. Across 66 run-metrics files and 126 saved candidate-probe records, the script recomputes paired utility and gain differences, null-adjusted property and structure probe advantages, and composite eligibility flags against the archived verification report (pilot records). All checks operate strictly on saved numerical outputs, and Table 2 summarises the resulting experimental units and failure counts. Qualified privacy breaches eliminate 13 candidates outright. Independent utility or remote-gain failures account for the remaining 6 configurations and leave zero viable splits under the frozen exploratory rules. Even if all 20 unqualified probes were rebuilt and passed calibration, newly qualified measurements could only add further breach flags without overturning any recorded rejection. Uncertainty estimators also differ structurally between the two campaigns. Exploratory cells apply two-sided 95% Student-t intervals over four independent seeds, whereas pilot utility gates enforce one-sided 95% upper Student-t bound (t0.95,2 = 2.919986) across three paired seeds. Both conventions remain distinct throughout our reanalysis scripts. Disjoint combinations of rejection causes appear separately in Table 4 (Appendix B) so readers can inspect exact failure overlaps without conflating heterogeneous confidence rules. Separating atomic probe readouts from composite campaign labels clarifies what happened inside the defence pilot. Atomic leakage stays visible. Every pilot cell recorded calibrated next-byte structure breaches (0.097 to 0.112, with all 21 of 21 seed bindings qualified) and qualified punctuation-property advantages (0.79 to 0.89), yet when one or two seed bindings for the punctuation-property probe stepped outside the 0.02 null band, the all-bindings rule labelled the composite cell undetermined even though concrete calibrated leakage was already measured. Figure 1 displays gate outcomes for both multi-cell campaigns side by side without collapsing their distinct reporting rules.

sections.title: 5.1 Attack success under broader access
sections.content: Adversary privileges govern when empirical attack outcomes transfer across threat models. simple monotonic relationship separates demonstrated breaches from empirical non-detections. Proposition 1 (Transfer under nested observations). Fix target distribution, recovery metric, and computational budget. Suppose observer receives every value visible to observer and can apply every budget-admissible attack for after projecting onto As observation space. There then exists budgetadmissible attack for whose expected recovery matches or exceeds that of any individual attack available to A. Non-detection by tested attack under places no non-trivial upper bound on recovery under B. Proof. Projecting Bs input onto As view and running As attack reproduces the exact output distribution and recovery score within budget. Existence of that projected attack leaves open whether particular gradient optimiser finds it, while failure of one tested attack under leaves stronger uses of Bs extra state unconstrained. Shared-key orthogonal wrapping illustrates why Proposition 1 invalidates careless threat-model upgrades (wrapper records). Multiplying hidden states by an orthogonal matrix transforms boundary traffic via = hQ, = hQT. (2) Who holds defines the security boundary. While passive network tap lacking sees rotated coordinates h, an authorised cloud server that stores or derives in host RAM to compute = hQT breaks the no-key premise immediately if compromised. Archived experiment accounts and collection manifests restrict the restoration result to passive wire and capture observers (wrapper records, deployment records). Recent attacks that invert statistical and permutation obfuscation in third-party LLM serving highlight the same host-exposure boundary [22]. 8 Orthogonal maps also preserve Euclidean norms and token inner products exactly. Coordinate mismatch explains why position-wise MLP decoder fails on while relational Gram geometry stays intact across the sequence. Stronger known-plaintext alignment solvers inside the robustness archive exploit labelled pairs to recover the subspace at depth-dependent sample sizes (wrapper records), consistent with independent findings that deeper transformer cuts retain recoverable internal states [4, 5, 13]. Aggregating sessions can obscure peak exposure as well (wrapper records). Under per-session rotation at depth 1, the pooled top-1 recovery score is 3.71%, yet constituent sessions reach 5.73%, 3.65%, and 2.34%. Pooled averages understate the leakiest session. Because known-plaintext solvers extract sensitive partial spans well below the absolute 50% crossing in Table 3, interpolated K50 brackets track empirical attack scaling in the lab without defining safe operational key lifetimes.

sections.title: 5.2 Comparing rotation cadences
sections.content: Archived deployment logs separate three-session Mistral-7B per-session rotation test from later eight-run Mistral-NeMo-12B per-epoch ratcheting matrix (deployment records). Per-session swaps add negligible latency. Within the 12B per-epoch matrix, greedy-decode identity holds in 20 of 24 sessions and four of the eight runs carry documented admissibility caveats, while the N=256 arm executes zero rotations across its 60-token decode horizon and acts as static control (though its zero-RTT throughput still drops from 7.67.7 to 6.36.4 tokens/s due to harness overhead). Wire decoders scored zero top-1 recovery on rotated epochs within that bounded capture setup. Frequent ratcheting imposes steep latency penalties (deployment records). At cadence N=16 with zero emulated RTT in session 1, recorded throughput drops from 7.6 tokens/s on the static baseline to 2.8 tokens/s under ratcheting (a 63.16% reduction at saved precision), whereas the evidence-triggered budget arm runs near 5.5 to 5.6 tokens/s at zero emulated RTT (and 2.6 to 2.9 tokens/s at 80 ms RTT). Model scale, rotation cadence, and RTT twins remain distinct experimental factors across those extracted logs. Provenance reconciliation explains why two internal documents disagreed about this matrix (deployment records). An early summary flagged the entire ratchet sweep invalid before subsequent RTT-twin review readmitted the supporting runs alongside explicit identity, throughput, and cloud-RAM key caveats. Following our precedence rule, we adopt the later collection manifest together with every attached operational restriction.

sections.title: 5.3 Reading mutual information estimates
sections.content: Companion boundary evaluations report near-zero Mutual Information Neural Estimation (MINE) [1] readouts on defended latent splits (MI-analysis records). For any measurable critic with finite expectations (EPXZ [T ] < and EPX PZ [eT ] < ), the population DonskerVaradhan variational objective obeys LT = EPXZ [T (X, Z)] log EPX PZ [eT (X,Z)] MI(X, Z), (3) where log is the natural logarithm and MI(X, Z) denotes true mutual information in nats. That inequality bounds leakage strictly from below. In addition to severe finite-sample bias and exponential variance in variational estimators [11, 21], Eq. (3) points in the wrong direction to certify an upper leakage budget, just as weak empirical attacks in differential-privacy auditing never prove small ε [7]. trivial analytic channel exposes the flaw immediately. Let input be uniform over discrete symbols, transmit plaintext = X, and evaluate constant critic = 0. Critic output LT equals zero identically even though MI(X, Z) = log nats (8 full bits at = 256). Pairing the MINE readout with second lower-bound estimator (such as the companion studys calibrated cross-entropy probe bound) leaves the inequality direction unchanged, and the companion drafts own limitations section acknowledges that neither estimator furnishes an upper bound (MI-analysis records). We therefore treat near-zero critic readouts as finite non-detections by particular neural family while leaving true channel leakage open in both directions. Architectural ablations require identical restraint (MI-analysis records). Observing comparable task metrics across handful of invariant MLP and radial remote modules demonstrates empirical saturation within the tested training budget, whereas proving universal information-theoretic capacity ceiling would require bounding every admissible remote function family.

sections.title: 6 Relationship to existing evidence and methods
sections.content: Split learning was originally introduced to train collaborative models without exporting raw client records [23], and recent surveys catalogue rapidly growing literature adapting split architectures to LLM fine-tuning [9]. Backward tensors still leak text. Modern reconstruction attacks recover private inputs from exchanged gradients and activations [27, 15, 12]. Within our examined programme, adding returned gradients in controlled GPT-2 benchmark lifts exact-document recovery from 13.71% to 37.77% while increasing token recovery by 3.17 pp [19], and client-returned loss gradients nullify synthetic decoys through exact-zero support masks [17]. Temporal gradient correlations leak trajectories through similar structural channels in reinforcement learning [2]. Here we retain each cited measurement under its original attribution and denominator. Methodological overlap with LLM-Attack Suite calls for clear boundaries [16]. That framework already specifies observation contracts, undefended controls, saved predictions, missing-attack disclosures, and harness checks. Our work operates one layer higher. By reconciling cross-campaign decision tables where qualified breaches, uncalibrated probes, shifted labels, and host-key assumptions collide, we isolate which programme-level conclusions survive without claiming diagnostic benchmarks on unseen external repositories. External studies warn repeatedly that weak evaluators manufacture false privacy. Wu et al. [24] break federated defences calibrated against static attacks, while Smith et al. [20] measure 1.16-fold to 6.59-fold higher leakage on FaceScrub under adaptive attack optimisation (and separately show that changing the external evaluators feature basis alters measured leakage). Threat-model and budget sensitivity appears across multimodal and LLM benchmarks as well [25, 10]. Layer-wise analyses independently confirm that deeper transformer splits retain recoverable internal states [4, 5, 13]. Evaluator scepticism still cuts only one way, because disqualifying 20 uncalibrated probes in our 19-cell exploration leaves all 13 breaches caught by the four calibrated probes intact. Recent defence studies reinforce both our host-custody and variational-bound findings. Jin et al. [8] show that perturbation alone struggles during federated split-LLM fine-tuning and propose client obfuscateand-recover adapters, Chen et al. [3] introduce mixup-based activation obfuscation for split LLMs, and Zhang et al. [26] investigate generative gradient masking in medical federated learning. Key custody remains decisive. Thomas et al. [22] invert permutation-based third-party LLM inference schemes and illustrate why invertible coordinate transforms demand explicit host-memory accounting. On the information-theoretic side, 10 Noorbakhsh et al. [14] apply mutual-information regularisation during collaborative split inference and Gu et al. [6] incorporate mutual-information regulariser during split-LLM fine-tuning, while formal statistical limits on neural mutual-information estimators [1, 11, 21], paired with empirical differential-privacy auditing [7], explain why near-zero critic scores never certify small upper leakage budgets.

sections.title: 7 Limitations and implications for further evaluation
sections.content: Selection and dependence. Case selection occurred retrospectively after all campaign outcomes had already been observed. Shared codebases, corpora, checkpoints, and design decisions link every episode inside one group. Archive tallies describe this collection alone, and measuring false-positive or false-negative classification rates on external papers would require prospectively registered validation cohort. Evidence available for recomputation. Executable scripts recompute seed contrasts, confidence bounds, and composite gate decisions wherever raw CSV or JSON arrays exist in the package. Some upstream artifacts remain source-reported. Decoy-gradient frame counts and portions of the boundary-replacement review come from their primary manuscripts and archived review verdicts without refitting attackers or rescoring tensor captures. File-level SHA-256 digests verify byte identity across all 122 consumed records, and untraced constants lacking primary calibration curve stay excluded. Qualification and uncertainty. Probe qualification binds strictly to one declared target, channel, defence mechanism, and budget. Seed cohorts remain small. Four-seed two-sided Student-t intervals in the exploration and three-seed one-sided upper bounds in the defence pilot condition on fixed evaluation panels without multiplicity adjustments, while the unexecuted eight-seed power figure serves purely as variance-sensitive planning bound. Positive-control canary floors, permutation-null bands, acceptance gates, and minimum detectable leak rates measure distinct properties even when two constants share the value 0.02. Security and utility. Empirical non-detection reflects bounded attacker and compute budget. Low pooled passive recovery, invertible wrappers whose keys sit in cloud RAM, and near-zero variational lower bounds leave compromised-host secrecy unproved. Utility gates cover only their scored endpoints, since short-context cross-entropy can pass while teacher-forced answer-token accuracy drops sharply, and evaluating noise or quantisation fairly requires sweeping perturbation strength against explicit task-quality caps. Explicit threat contracts enable testable future benchmarks. Deliberately injected channel omissions and label shifts can run alongside genuinely leaky defences under frozen compute budgets. Prospective validation trials on held-out model families and corpora can then quantify how reliably automated admissibility checks catch false privacy assurance while preserving confirmed breaches.

sections.title: 8 Conclusion
sections.content: Re-examining six linked investigations from one split-LLM programme separates broken measurements from broken defences. Two early assurances failed on method. Omitted client-returned gradients and off-by-one token labels undermined those initial claims, yet 13 qualified breaches in the 19-cell exploration alongside 40 punctuation-property excesses and 5 next-byte structure excesses in the seven-cell pilot stand as sound negative evidence against the tested defences despite incomplete probe qualification elsewhere. Scope checks likewise confine shared-key orthogonal wrappers to passive network links, document the 63.16% throughput penalty of rapid per-epoch ratcheting, and show why variational mutual-information lower bounds near zero leave true leakage unconstrained above. Tying every privacy verdict to its observed channels, key custody, 11 calibrated controls, and seed-level uncertainty establishes exactly what archived split-training experiments support. Data and code availability. The manuscript source, reanalysis scripts, derived tables, and archived evidence reside in the companion repository at https://github.com/setloop-io/Separating-MeasurementFailures-from-Defence-Failures-in-Split-Language-Model-Privacy [18]. Python recomputation scripts live under analysis/, derived tables and SHA-256 input manifests under data/, LaTeX sources and vector figure generators under paper/, and primary records under evidence/ and reproduction/. Appendix maps each retained statistic to its exact repository-relative path. Every consistency check runs offline on the Python standard library without GPU retraining.
